newsitem.title: LEBANON: Head of Lebanon's constitutional court resigns.
newsitem.headline: Head of Lebanon's constitutional court resigns.

text.p: The head of Lebanon's Constitutional Council has offered his resignation, shortly before it is due to rule on 19 appeals against the results of last summer's parliamentary elections.
Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri read Judge Wajdi al-Mallat's resignation letter to parliament on Thursday.

"I officially announce my resignation from the presidency and membership of the (Constitutional) council. I submit this resignation to parliament which appointed me a member of this council," the letter said.
It was not immediately clear whether Mallat's resignation had been accepted by parliament.
Supporters of the Syrian-backed government won an overwhelming majority in the 128-member parliament in the five-stage elections which ended on September 15, 1996.
Eighteen defeated candidates lodged appeals with the Constitutional Council against the election results, charging corruption and intimidation.
They demanded that the court overturn the results of their individual contests and declare them winners. A 19th candidate demanded cancellation of the entire election.
Politicians and newspapers say the council's rulings on the appeals are expected by mid-April when half of its 10 members are to be replaced by rotation.
The council can cancel the election of individual deputies and award their seats to other candidates if it decides serious fraud existed.
